questions.prompt: Which article marker is used before a singular proper name of a person (e.g. '___ Maria')?
questions.explanation: 'Si' is used before a singular proper noun of a person (e.g. Si Maria ay maganda).

questions.prompt: Which article marker is used before two or more proper names of people (e.g. '___ Juan at Pedro')?
questions.explanation: 'Sina' is the plural proper noun marker used before multiple names.

questions.prompt: Which article is used before a singular common noun (e.g. 'the house')?
questions.explanation: 'Ang' is the singular common noun article marker in Tagalog.

questions.prompt: How do you form the plural of a common noun like 'bata' (child)?
questions.explanation: 'Ang mga' is placed before a common noun to make it plural.

questions.prompt: Translate 'The house is big' into predicate-first (inverted) word order without 'ay': ______
questions.explanation: In Tagalog inverted word order, the predicate (adjective) comes first, followed by 'ang' and the subject.

questions.prompt: What is the plural form of the adjective 'mabait' (kind)?
questions.explanation: Tagalog adjectives form their plural by duplicating the first syllable of the root word (bait -> mababait).

questions.prompt: What is the plural form of the adjective 'maganda' (beautiful/pretty)? ______
questions.explanation: Root: ganda. First syllable of root 'ga' is duplicated: ma-ga-ganda.

questions.prompt: In standard traditional word order (Subject + ay + Predicate), how do you say 'The dog is big'?
questions.explanation: Traditional word order puts subject + 'ay' + predicate: 'Ang aso ay malaki.'
